China’s Chemicals Sector Posts Modest Growth Amidst Stable Market Conditions

China’s chemicals industry reported steady growth for the first quarter, buoyed by resilient downstream demand and relatively stable input costs, according to figures released on Thursday by the National Association of Chemical Enterprises (NACE). The results highlight the sector’s continued recovery following a challenging 2023, with executives expressing cautious optimism for the remainder of the year.

Aggregate revenue for the industry reached RMB 2.1 trillion in the first three months of 2024, a 3.7% increase year-on-year. NACE attributed the growth to sustained demand from key sectors such as construction, automotive components, and consumer goods, as well as incremental improvements in export performance. Total chemical output rose 2.9% from the same period last year, while the average operating margin for the sector edged up to 7.8%.

“Stable domestic consumption, alongside a gradual rebound in export orders, has provided a solid foundation for the industry this quarter,” said Zhou Ming, NACE’s deputy secretary-general, during a press briefing in Beijing. “While some segments remain under pressure from global price competition, the sector as a whole is benefiting from improved supply chain efficiencies and moderate input prices.”

Leading producers, including Huasheng Petrochemicals and Oriental Synthesis Group, reported solid sales of basic chemicals, polymers, and specialty materials. Executives at Huasheng cited “robust demand for construction-grade resins” as a key driver, while Oriental Synthesis pointed to “steady orders from the packaging and electronics industries.”

Industry analysts noted that favorable energy prices, alongside stable supplies of raw materials, helped manufacturers maintain healthy operating rates. “The absence of major disruptions or volatility in feedstock markets has enabled companies to focus on optimizing production and logistics,” said Liu Qiang, an analyst at SinoAsia Securities.

Meanwhile, the government maintained existing environmental compliance standards, with no significant policy changes affecting the sector during the reporting period. Commenting on the outlook, NACE’s Zhou Ming observed, “We expect the current trajectory to hold, provided downstream demand remains resilient and external conditions do not change materially.”

China’s chemicals industry employs over 7 million workers and remains a crucial pillar of the nation’s industrial economy. The sector’s performance is closely watched as a barometer of broader manufacturing activity. As the year progresses, companies are expected to continue investing in product innovation and production upgrades to enhance competitiveness in both domestic and global markets.
